notes:
Summary: Copperridge Conversio is a mid-market SaaS provider for customer-facing ticketing and knowledge; CTO (Anya Torres) and Head of CX (Marcus Liu) are sponsors. Primary objective: reduce live-agent volume via RAG-powered deflection and provide agent context cards for faster resolution. They ingest 18M historical tickets + KB articles (~40M doc shards after chunking).

Technical requirements (high level):
- Index scale: targeting 20-50M shards, incremental daily delta ~50k tickets.
- Retrieval latency SLO: 95th <= 200ms for embedding-based candidate fetch; end-to-end suggestion (embedding + rerank + display) <= 600ms for agent UX, <= 350ms for customer self-serve microflow (chat widget).
- Desired top-5 precision: reranker must push relevant doc into top-5 > 92% on internal eval sets.
- Cost target: blended cost per query (embeddings + rerank + model tokens) < $0.03 for self-serve deflection, < $0.08 for agent-assist richer responses.
- Model preferences: open LLMs for reranking and re-ranking-friendly quantized models for cost control; fallback to smaller SFT or instruction-tuned reranker when latency tight.
- Routing: multi-tier routing by customer tier and latency vs cost tradeoffs; automatic fallback to cached answers and smaller models under load.
- Security: VPC private endpoints, SSO/SAML, KMS for key management, audit logs, 7-year retention for compliance (EU customers).

Recent activity / timeline: 
- 2024-09-12: Lead created from Integrations webinar (Jordan P).
- 2024-09-25: Intro call (AE Jordan + SE Riley) w/ CTO Anya, Head CX Marcus. Demo of hosted API; expressed interest in Dedicated for predictable latency.
- 2024-10-10: Technical deep-dive (SE) + data sizing session. Provided sample embedding cost calc.
- 2024-10-22: POC kickoff: Copperridge provided 500k anonymized tickets for initial index and eval.
- 2024-11-02: Fireflies call (ff_20241102_3271) — Marcus: "we need answers in under half a second or agents lose flow". Riley recorded runbook notes.
- 2024-11-18: First POC run: 2-stage pipeline (dense retrieval -> cross-encoder reranker). Observed retrieval 95p ~ 180ms (single shard cluster), rerank adds 220-300ms depending on model size. Composite E2E median ~420ms.
- 2024-11-25: Cost simulation: projected $0.045/q for current reranker; exceeds target for high-volume. Discussed quantized reranker and batching.
- 2024-12-04: Internal exec review at Copperridge; ask for SLA language and a pricing runbook for 3 scenarios (hosted, dedicated reserved, private).

POC findings (SE notes):
- Dense index using Faiss HNSW + 384-d embeddings gives solid recall; CPU-bound ANN lookups are <120ms at target shard count when pinned on dedicated infra.
- Cross-encoder reranker (bi-encoder candidate -> cross-encoder re-score) yields best top-5 quality but current model sizing causes 200-350ms overhead. Quantized 8-bit cross-encoders reduce latency ~30% but small drop in top-5 precision (~2.5 points).
- Caching prefix and KV results for frequent queries reduces calls by 18% in simulated traffic.

Commercial / procurement notes:
- Copperridge prefers monthly/annual pricing with committed qps for Dedicated. Want clear migration path from hosted -> dedicated -> private. Legal requests data residency addendum for EU customers.
- Decision influencers: CTO Anya (technical fit), Head CX Marcus (business case: reduce live transfers by 30%), Procurement lead Sofia (price sensitivity).

Quotes & soundbites:
- Marcus Liu: "If the assistant has to wait, agents open an existing ticket — inertia kills deflection."
- Anya Torres: "We can't sacrifice top-5 quality for marginal latency wins; customers notice incorrect suggestions."

Next steps (short):
- Redwood: deliver detailed perf vs cost matrix for 3 reranker configurations (cross-encoder full, quantized cross-encoder, distilled cross-encoder) by 2024-12-12.
- Copperridge: legal to share required wording for data residency by 2024-12-18.
- Joint: schedule SLA/legal sync + pricing workbook review (owner Jordan).

Blockers: legal/data residency + uncertainty about how quantization affects top-5 rerank threshold. Pricing threshold must hit $0.03 for self-serve or Copperridge will push more aggressive caching + cheaper models which may reduce deflection rates.
